notes.text: Let's start with a couple establishing shots of space. Maybe it's, and it's going to be drifting. So maybe we start with a borrowed establishing shot of the planet, the moons, and some cosmic stuff, maybe even meteor racing by. And we're going to drift into frame, cut into the interior of the spaceship. The air will fade into, or will drift over into Harper's profile coming in and locking the stars. We're going to do something kind of dramatic here. When we get to her floating, we don't want to see her body out because we want to bounce back out to see that she's floating. I wonder if we can do this. Maybe that we get tiresome as kind of a runner where we connect all the transitions with either a speed zoom or an actual camera movement to the next cut. That would probably be hard. Consistency would probably be tough. Maybe we can do that where we can do that in a few places though. Just be tiring to try and keep it up for the whole thing. Maybe for select scenes and cuts between the scenes we can do that.

Here is where we should start seeing Harper's face sort of come into frame, drift in. She's floating in, sort of like her face is almost eclipsing the, I don't know, I would get too metaphorical here, but her face is coming in, floating into frame and it's in the foreground. I don't know if we have to do a pole focus, like start with a too far in focus to actually be, maybe a little hard to pull off with a focus with a graphic novel style rendering, yet at the same time, maybe a little confusing to see her face come in, maybe not in front of the foreground, unless there's something in between to give some sense of scale so you can tell that she's not just kind of planet-sized head or anything like that.

Here we want to pull out the camera and not to see that she's floating inside her spaceship. And we want to make sure this is really, the scenery is just awesome, just eye catching. We want to set up the blocking and the camera and everything in the scene to be just kind of an awesome in orbit over a planet shot of all this cosmic glory.

Here, on a way up here, up above, we want to do a quick zoom out, like a speed blur zoom out to get a better scene, not so far that we can't make out the exterior of the spaceship clearly, and still seeing Harper inside, but giving us a bigger sense of scale. I wonder if we can have something else going on in the background just to keep things interesting. We wanted to distract from the scale as well. Maybe there's something happening in terms of the sun coming up over the horizon or something, or there's a change that would give us lighting effects, or something that would be interesting in the scene.

At this point, we will actually change to a new scene. This is where we're explaining the walls and the windows and stuff. So we'll cut back to the interior. Maybe it's not facing towards the planet anymore. We're doing a space side shot. So we're shooting through and she is and we're seeing her. So she's looking towards the planet. But she's got her hands on the glass. She's folded up close so she can get a closer look even though it's not going to be much of a change perspective from her being in the center or being touching the glass. We just want to come up with something that makes it, illustrates that the walls and windows that we're talking about are this sphere of the spaceship.
On to the big world, to the big big world below we want to maybe pull out to show the world down below
Here we're getting a close up of her face right close to the sphere where maybe we can see cosmic things reflected in her eyes.

cut to showing harper interacting projected holograph 3d display that can be summand to materialize in the ship interior showing a sort of schematic diagram of the star system with helpful outlines with labels and interaction points she can use with her fingers. She interacts with the display to zoom out from the planet she's orbiting to the whole star system and then out to the local stars fairly quickly to show start hinting at the scale of things

And for here we show her realizing that compared to the endless expanse of space, her ship is a very small space and she makes an expression like she'd like to get out of there and experience the real size of space
